CREATE TABLE `event` (
    `event_id` TEXT, -- A unique identifier for the event; example: ['rec0Si5cQ4rJRVzd6', 'rec0akZnLLpGUloLH']
    `event_name` TEXT, -- event name; example: ['March Meeting', 'Officers meeting - January']
    `event_date` TEXT, -- The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; example: ['2020-03-10T12:00:00', '2020-01-14T09:30:00']
    `type` TEXT, -- The kind of event, such as game, social, election; example: ['Meeting', 'Election']
    `notes` TEXT, -- A free text field for any notes about the event; example: ['All active members can vote for new officers between 4pm-8pm.', "Attend Women's soccer game as a group."]
    `location` TEXT, -- Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location; example: ['MU 215', 'Campus Soccer/Lacrosse stadium']
    `status` TEXT, -- One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; example: ['Open', 'Planning']
    PRIMARY KEY (`event_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `major` (
    `major_id` TEXT, -- A unique identifier for each major; example: ['rec06DF6vZ1CyPKpc', 'rec09LedkREyskCNv']
    `major_name` TEXT, -- major name; example: ['Outdoor Product Design and Development', 'Agricultural Communication']
    `department` TEXT, -- The name of the department that offers the major; example: ['School of Applied Sciences, Technology and Education', 'Watershed Sciences Department']
    `college` TEXT, -- The name college that houses the department that offers the major; example: ['College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences', 'College of Natural Resources']
    PRIMARY KEY (`major_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `zip_code` (
    `zip_code` INTEGER, -- The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.; example: [501, 544]
    `type` TEXT, -- The kind of ZIP code; example: ['Unique', 'Standard']
    `city` TEXT, -- The city to which the ZIP pertains; example: ['Holtsville', 'Adjuntas']
    `county` TEXT, -- The county to which the ZIP pertains; example: ['Suffolk County', 'Adjuntas Municipio']
    `state` TEXT, -- The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains; example: ['New York', 'Puerto Rico']
    `short_state` TEXT, -- The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains; example: ['NY', 'PR']
    PRIMARY KEY (`zip_code`)
);

CREATE TABLE `attendance` (
    `link_to_event` TEXT, -- The unique identifier of the event which was attended; example: ['rec2N69DMcrqN9PJC']
    `link_to_member` TEXT, -- The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; example: ['recD078PnS3x2doBe', 'recP6DJPyi5donvXL']
    PRIMARY KEY (`link_to_event`, `link_to_member`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_member`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_event`) REFERENCES `event` (`event_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `budget` (
    `budget_id` TEXT, -- A unique identifier for the budget entry; example: ['rec0QmEc3cSQFQ6V2', 'rec1bG6HSft7XIvTP']
    `category` TEXT, -- The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking; example: ['Advertisement', 'Food']
    `spent` REAL, -- The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; example: [67.81, 121.14]
    `remaining` REAL, -- A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; example: [7.19, 28.86]
    `amount` INTEGER, -- The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; example: [75, 150]
    `event_status` TEXT, -- the status of the event; example: ['Closed', 'Open']
    `link_to_event` TEXT, -- The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; example: ['recI43CzsZ0Q625ma', 'recggMW2eyCYceNcy']
    PRIMARY KEY (`budget_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_event`) REFERENCES `event` (`event_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `expense` (
    `expense_id` TEXT, -- unique id of income; example: ['rec017x6R3hQqkLAo', 'rec1nIjoZKTYayqZ6']
    `expense_description` TEXT, -- A textual description of what the money was spend for; example: ['Post Cards, Posters', 'Water, Cookies']
    `expense_date` TEXT, -- The date the expense was incurred; example: ['2019-08-20', '2019-10-08']
    `cost` REAL, -- The dollar amount of the expense; example: [122.06, 20.2]
    `approved` TEXT, -- A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; example: ['true']
    `link_to_member` TEXT, -- The member who incurred the expense; example: ['rec4BLdZHS2Blfp4v', 'recro8T1MPMwRadVH']
    `link_to_budget` TEXT, -- The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given catego; example: ['recvKTAWAFKkVNnXQ', 'recy8KY5bUdzF81vv']
    PRIMARY KEY (`expense_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_member`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_budget`) REFERENCES `budget` (`budget_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `income` (
    `income_id` TEXT, -- A unique identifier for each record of income; example: ['rec0s9ZrO15zhzUeE', 'rec7f5XMQZexgtQJo']
    `date_received` TEXT, -- the date that the fund received; example: ['2019-10-17', '2019-09-04']
    `amount` INTEGER, -- amount of funds; example: [50]
    `source` TEXT, -- A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation; example: ['Dues']
    `notes` TEXT, -- A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds; example: []
    `link_to_member` TEXT, -- link to member; example: ['reccW7q1KkhSKZsea', 'recTjHY5xXhvkCdVT']
    PRIMARY KEY (`income_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_member`) REFERENCES `member` (`member_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `member` (
    `member_id` TEXT, -- unique id of member; example: ['rec1x5zBFIqoOuPW8', 'rec280Sk7o31iG0Tx']
    `first_name` TEXT, -- member's first name; example: ['Angela', 'Grant']
    `last_name` TEXT, -- member's last name; example: ['Sanders', 'Gilmour']
    `email` TEXT, -- member's email; example: ['angela.sanders@lpu.edu', 'grant.gilmour@lpu.edu']
    `position` TEXT, -- The position the member holds in the club; example: ['Member', 'Inactive']
    `t_shirt_size` TEXT, -- The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; example: ['Medium', 'X-Large']
    `phone` TEXT, -- The best telephone at which to contact the member; example: ['(651) 928-4507', '403-555-1310']
    `zip` INTEGER, -- the zip code of the member's hometown; example: [55108, 29440]
    `link_to_major` TEXT, -- The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table; example: ['recxK3MHQFbR9J5uO', 'rec7BxKpjJ7bNph3O']
    PRIMARY KEY (`member_id`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`zip`) REFERENCES `zip_code` (`zip_code`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`link_to_major`) REFERENCES `major` (`major_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `circuits` (
    `circuitId` INTEGER, -- unique identification number of the circuit; example: [2, 3]
    `circuitRef` TEXT, -- circuit reference name; example: ['sepang', 'bahrain']
    `name` TEXT, -- full name of circuit; example: ['Sepang International Circuit', 'Bahrain International Circuit']
    `location` TEXT, -- location of circuit; example: ['Kuala Lumpur', 'Sakhir']
    `country` TEXT, -- country of circuit; example: ['Malaysia', 'Bahrain']
    `lat` REAL, -- latitude of location of circuit; example: [2.76083, 26.0325]
    `lng` REAL, -- longitude of location of circuit; example: [101.738, 50.5106]
    `alt` INTEGER, -- example: []
    `url` TEXT, -- url; example: ['http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepang_International_Circuit', 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain_International_Circuit']
    PRIMARY KEY (`circuitId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructors` (
    `constructorId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying constructors; example: [1, 2]
    `constructorRef` TEXT, -- Constructor Reference name; example: ['mclaren', 'bmw_sauber']
    `name` TEXT, -- full name of the constructor; example: ['McLaren', 'BMW Sauber']
    `nationality` TEXT, -- nationality of the constructor; example: ['British', 'German']
    `url` TEXT, -- the introduction website of the constructor; example: ['http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren', 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Sauber']
    PRIMARY KEY (`constructorId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `drivers` (
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying each driver; example: [1, 2]
    `driverRef` TEXT, -- driver reference name; example: ['hamilton', 'heidfeld']
    `number` INTEGER, -- number; example: [44, 6]
    `code` TEXT, -- abbreviated code for drivers; example: ['HAM', 'HEI']
    `forename` TEXT, -- forename; example: ['Lewis', 'Nick']
    `surname` TEXT, -- surname; example: ['Hamilton', 'Heidfeld']
    `dob` DATE, -- date of birth; example: ['1985-01-07', '1977-05-10']
    `nationality` TEXT, -- nationality of drivers; example: ['British', 'German']
    `url` TEXT, -- the introduction website of the drivers; example: ['http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton', 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Heidfeld']
    PRIMARY KEY (`driverId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `seasons` (
    `year` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying the race; example: [1950, 1951]
    `url` TEXT, -- website link of season race introduction; example: ['http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_Formula_One_season', 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1951_Formula_One_season']
    PRIMARY KEY (`year`)
);

CREATE TABLE `races` (
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying the race; example: [2, 3]
    `year` INTEGER, -- year; example: [2009]
    `round` INTEGER, -- round; example: [2, 3]
    `circuitId` INTEGER, -- circuit Id; example: [2, 17]
    `name` TEXT, -- name of the race; example: ['Malaysian Grand Prix', 'Chinese Grand Prix']
    `date` DATE, -- duration time; example: ['2009-04-05', '2009-04-19']
    `time` TEXT, -- time of the location; example: ['09:00:00', '07:00:00']
    `url` TEXT, -- introduction of races; example: ['http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Malaysian_Grand_Prix', 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Chinese_Grand_Prix']
    PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`circuitId`) REFERENCES `circuits` (`circuitId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`year`) REFERENCES `seasons` (`year`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructorResults` (
    `constructorResultsId` INTEGER, -- constructor Results Id; example: [1, 2]
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- race id; example: [18]
    `constructorId` INTEGER, -- constructor id; example: [1, 2]
    `points` REAL, -- points; example: [14.0, 8.0]
    `status` TEXT, -- status; example: []
    PRIMARY KEY (`constructorResultsId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`constructorId`) REFERENCES `constructors` (`constructorId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `constructorStandings` (
    `constructorStandingsId` INTEGER, -- unique identification of the constructor standing records; example: [1, 2]
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- id number identifying which races; example: [18]
    `constructorId` INTEGER, -- id number identifying which id; example: [1, 2]
    `points` REAL, -- how many points acquired in each race; example: [14.0, 8.0]
    `position` INTEGER, -- position or track of circuits; example: [1, 3]
    `positionText` TEXT, -- position text; example: ['1', '3']
    `wins` INTEGER, -- wins; example: [1, 0]
    PRIMARY KEY (`constructorStandingsId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`constructorId`) REFERENCES `constructors` (`constructorId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `driverStandings` (
    `driverStandingsId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying driver standing records; example: [1, 2]
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- id number identifying which races; example: [18]
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- id number identifying which drivers; example: [1, 2]
    `points` REAL, -- how many points acquired in each race; example: [10.0, 8.0]
    `position` INTEGER, -- position or track of circuits; example: [1, 2]
    `positionText` TEXT, -- position text; example: ['1', '2']
    `wins` INTEGER, -- wins; example: [1, 0]
    PRIMARY KEY (`driverStandingsId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`driverId`) REFERENCES `drivers` (`driverId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `lapTimes` (
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying race; example: [2]
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying each driver; example: [1]
    `lap` INTEGER, -- lap number; example: [1, 2]
    `position` INTEGER, -- position or track of circuits; example: [10, 11]
    `time` TEXT, -- lap time; example: ['1:52.965', '1:41.865']
    `milliseconds` INTEGER, -- milliseconds; example: [112965, 101865]
    PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`, `driverId`, `lap`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`driverId`) REFERENCES `drivers` (`driverId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `pitStops` (
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying race; example: [842]
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying each driver; example: [1, 2]
    `stop` INTEGER, -- stop number; example: [1, 2]
    `lap` INTEGER, -- lap number; example: [12, 24]
    `time` TEXT, -- time; example: ['16:24:40', '16:45:48']
    `duration` TEXT, -- duration time; example: ['22.552', '22.611']
    `milliseconds` INTEGER, -- milliseconds; example: [22552, 22611]
    PRIMARY KEY (`raceId`, `driverId`, `stop`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`driverId`) REFERENCES `drivers` (`driverId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `qualifying` (
    `qualifyId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying qualifying; example: [23, 24]
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying each race; example: [19]
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying each driver; example: [13, 8]
    `constructorId` INTEGER, -- constructor Id; example: [6, 1]
    `number` INTEGER, -- number; example: [2, 1]
    `position` INTEGER, -- position or track of circuit; example: [1, 2]
    `q1` TEXT, -- time in qualifying 1; example: ['1:35.347', '1:35.645']
    `q2` TEXT, -- time in qualifying 2; example: ['1:34.412', '1:34.188']
    `q3` TEXT, -- time in qualifying 3; example: ['1:35.748', '1:36.230']
    PRIMARY KEY (`qualifyId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`constructorId`) REFERENCES `constructors` (`constructorId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`driverId`) REFERENCES `drivers` (`driverId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `status` (
    `statusId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying status; example: [1, 2]
    `status` TEXT, -- full name of status; example: ['Finished', 'Disqualified']
    PRIMARY KEY (`statusId`)
);

CREATE TABLE `results` (
    `resultId` INTEGER, -- the unique identification number identifying race result; example: [23, 24]
    `raceId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying the race; example: [19]
    `driverId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying the driver; example: [8, 9]
    `constructorId` INTEGER, -- the identification number identifying which constructors; example: [6, 2]
    `number` INTEGER, -- number; example: [1, 4]
    `grid` INTEGER, -- the number identifying the area where cars are set into a grid formation in order to start the race.; example: [2, 4]
    `position` INTEGER, -- The finishing position or track of circuits; example: [1, 2]
    `positionText` TEXT, -- position text; example: ['1', '2']
    `positionOrder` INTEGER, -- the finishing order of positions; example: [1, 2]
    `points` REAL, -- points; example: [10.0, 8.0]
    `laps` INTEGER, -- lap number; example: [56]
    `time` TEXT, -- finish time; example: ['1:31:18.555', '+19.570']
    `milliseconds` INTEGER, -- the actual finishing time of drivers in milliseconds; example: [5478555, 5498125]
    `fastestLap` INTEGER, -- fastest lap number; example: [37, 39]
    `rank` INTEGER, -- starting rank positioned by fastest lap speed; example: [2, 6]
    `fastestLapTime` TEXT, -- fastest Lap Time; example: ['1:35.405', '1:35.921']
    `fastestLapSpeed` TEXT, -- fastest Lap Speed; example: ['209.158', '208.033']
    `statusId` INTEGER, -- status ID; example: [1]
    PRIMARY KEY (`resultId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`statusId`) REFERENCES `status` (`statusId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`constructorId`) REFERENCES `constructors` (`constructorId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`driverId`) REFERENCES `drivers` (`driverId`),
    FOREIGN KEY (`raceId`) REFERENCES `races` (`raceId`)
);
